result:
Solution 3 cannot be right. A quadratic rational map has automorphism group at most S₃ (nonabelian only if it is exactly S₃). So the tetrahedral group A₄ does not occur, and the claimed answer of 10 comes from a false classification.

Solution 1 builds its count from an orbit-decomposition argument that does not hold up. It assumes the three fixed points form one S₃-orbit and the six period-3 points form a single orbit, and these assumptions are not justified. The resulting total of 12 is unsupported.

Solution 2 correctly identifies Aut(f) ≅ S₃ and the geometric model 1/z². In that model the rational preperiodic points include 0, ∞, 1 and −1, which gives 4. Its claim that no twist can exceed this is asserted without proof, so I am not certain the maximum is 4. It is the most plausible of the three.

I could not recall the literature value with confidence. This choice rests on eliminating Solutions 1 and 3 rather than on a full derivation.

CHOICE: 2
